rationale.hitl-workflow: Coins bounded delegation pattern to preserve human craft via explicit authority scoping.
rationale.oversight-scaling-inversion: Highlights the right-shift problem where verification bottlenecks accelerating AI code generation.
rationale.oversight-explanation: Demands uncertainty signaling and inline explanations as core guardrails for AI outputs.
rationale.provenance-auditability: Proposes decision context systems and persistent provenance records for human reviewability.
rationale.ai-review: Reports empirical demand for context-aware AI pull request review assistants.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Reports empirical demand for change-aware AI test generation and quality gates.
rationale.quality-debt: Identifies the accumulation of AI-induced technical debt from the right-shift problem.
rationale.regulatory-compliance: Reports empirical demand for compiling audit evidence and interpreting policy requirements.
rationale.survey-input: Survey of 860 developers details desired AI tools and workflow constraints.
rationale.intro-framing: Sets a design agenda for 22 AI systems based on developer needs.
rationale.counterpoint: Argues against automation-first approaches, advocating for bounded delegation instead.
rationale.method-self-report: Analyzed open-ended responses from a survey of 860 Microsoft developers.
rationale.risk-quality: Reports empirical result: developers demand proactive regression warnings and quality gates.
rationale.risk-security: Reports empirical result: developers demand pre-merge security advisors with patch suggestions.
rationale.assistive: Proposes assistive tools like drafting workbenches and interactive exploration boards.
rationale.agentic: Proposes agentic tools like autonomous test generation and PR review assistants.
